- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Overestimates early in the forecast window when prices are trending upward, then underestimates later when prices stabilize or reverse.
- Shows significant lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts remain low for several days after a spike occurs.
- Tends to overshoot after sharp price increases, then corrects downward, suggesting a mean-reversion bias.
- Underestimates the magnitude of price increases in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, especially during sustained upward trends.
- Overconfident in short-term forecasts; fails to account for volatility clustering or policy-driven price shocks.
- Fails to capture the full impact of policy changes or market interventions in the immediate aftermath, leading to persistent underestimation.
- Model exhibits a “smoothness” bias — overly conservative in adjusting forecasts, avoiding sharp turns in price behavior.
